To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IncP-1 beta plasmid p8 carries a new transposition element and a class 1 integrin but transfers poorly to E. coli.

the IncP-1 beta plasmid p8, isolated from sewage treatment plants, is closely related to R751 but transfers to E. coli at low frequencies and that pB8 contains a new transposase encoding a small multidug resistance efflux protein.

the plasmid p8, which is closely related to IncP-1 beta plasmid R 751, is transferable to Escherichiacoli by conjugation, however at low frequencies and only under specific conditions, a phenomenon which is very unusual for plasmids of this group.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular characterization of a novel IncP-1 beta plasmid pBR8 that carries a new Tn5501 derivative, a Tn5090/402 derivative, and an unusual class 1 integon and that is closely related to plasmid R-751.
the identification of the genetic determinants that allow the IncP-1 beta plasmid R51 to replicate in Escherichia Coli.
the molecular analysis of a plasmid that is related to the prototype plasmid of the IncP-1 group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pB8 plasmid backbone is closely related to that of the R751 prototype but carries an accessory region with a new Tn5501 derivative and a Tn5090/402 element that are responsible for the amoxicillin and spectinomycin/streptomycin resistances of pB8.
pB8 is a typical IncP- 1beta plasmide but it is not a typical IncP plasmid since it is not transferable to E.coli.
the plasmid p8 carries a new transposable element, which is related to Tn550, and that the transfer properties of p8 is not due to the transposable element, but to the presence of a class 1 integer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pB8 is a typical IncP- beta plasmid but with a different set of accessory genes and that the poor transfer of the plasmids to E. coli is not due to these differences.
pB8 is a novel IncP-1 beta plasmid that is closely related to R751, but carries a new transposable element, Tn5501, and a new class 1 integro

plasmids pB10 and pB8, isolated in the 1980s and 1990s from sewage plants in Germany, are IncP-1 beta plasmids carrying a Tn5501-like element and a Tn5090/ Tn402 element with a class I integron, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pB8 and its relatives may represent a distinct subgroup of the IncP-1 family of plasmids that are closely related to R751, but that are not able to transfer to E. coliby conjugation.
the IncP-1 family of plasmids is much more diverse in terms of their accessory genetic content than previously thought.
